Same-Year Hires in Same Department (Self Join)

MediumFreeQuerying BasicsJoinsDate Functions

An onboarding analyst wants to identify employees who joined the same department in the same year — natural peer cohorts for ramp comparisons. Use a self join.

Show emp_a, emp_b, department, hire_year. Each pair should appear once (not mirrored) — use e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id to enforce one-direction pairing. Order by hire_year, department, emp_a.

The < trick is the standard way to deduplicate pairs in a self join. Without it you'd get both (Alice, Bob) and (Bob, Alice) for every pair, which is twice the noise.

Solve it in the browser editor →

Runs on SQLite in your browser, graded against the expected result, no signup. A wrong answer gets a diagnosis, not just "incorrect".

Schema

employees

emp_idnamedepartmentpositionsalaryhire_datemanager_idperformance_rating
1Alice JohnsonEngineeringSenior Developer950002019-03-1554.5
2Bob SmithEngineeringDeveloper750002020-06-0113.8
3Carol WilliamsMarketingMarketing Manager850002018-09-20NULL4.2

Expected output: Alice | Bob | Engineering | 2020

Hint

FROM employees e1 JOIN employees e2 ON e1.department = e2.department AND strftime('%Y', e1.hire_date) = strftime('%Y', e2.hire_date) WHERE e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id. The id-inequality kills mirror pairs.
